chapter: Countess Johnson's band and the Kansas City scene
title: Oliver Todd's high school band and the start of Countess Johnson's band
summary: Oliver Todd's band was taken over by Charlie Green, so five members formed a band with Countess Johnson on 12th Street.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Now in about late '33, Oliver Todd organized his little high school band. And at first, we had a male guy playing piano with us. I was much older than those guys, you know. But they'd come and get me out of the college, and I'd go down with my bass horn and we'd practice all those

things. And we had some gigs, you know And then the male singer left, and we got the girl singer, in Oliver Todd's group there. And somehow, he got an old alto player named Charlie Green, who had been in Clarence Love's band. And almost overnight, Charlie Green stole the band from Oliver Todd. We stayed with the band maybe a couple of weeks. So five of us just decided, since we're doing this-- by this time, it had become, like in '35, you know.
And we went out and got a job at this club on 12th Street.
What was the name of it?
Just Countess Johnson and Her Band, you know. We use her, and she took that boy, played in Oliver Todd's group, and so we used her, now, as a mediator in this thing, which made us a good draw.
Oh. So, how big would the band be now?
Five pieces. We used Now, there's William Scott
In fact, I was instrumental in bringing all the rest of them into Max Hand's (phonetic) band. McShann
